content.text:
Based on my review of the diff:

**CaptureTriage.tsx / uploadScreenshot**: The extracted upload function takes `uploadUrl` from a trusted Convex mutation (`generateUploadUrl`) and passes `file.type` as Content-Type — no attacker-controlled sink. The parsed `storageId` flows to `createCapture` which validates server-side. No injection.

**Error messages via `flashActionError`**: Static strings only (`"Could not save -- try again"`, `"Could not skip -- try again"`) — the caught error object is discarded, so no PII/token/URL leaks to UI.

**`busy` gate on save/skip**: Prevents double-submission; a fix, not a vuln. Guards all peer buttons (`btn-primary`, `btn-ghost triage-skip`, both Save variants, saveWithContext) — sibling-path parity holds.

**`uploadFailures` counter**: Just an integer count. No sensitive data exposed.

**Timeout refs (`leavingTimeoutRef`, `actionErrorTimeoutRef`)**: Properly cleared on unmount; no reference to persisted secrets.

**PersonSky.tsx**: Purely `memo` wrapper around presentational SVG — no security surface.

**SearchAdd.tsx**: Adds a 300ms delayed skeleton — no new data flow, no sinks.

**Test file**: Test-only; ignored per instructions.

No auth boundaries, no shell/SQL/eval/path/URL sinks, no allowlist/gate changes, no observability leaks, no registry fan-out. The change is UX polish, error handling, and test scaffolding.
